title: Reuse, Composition, and Orchestration
definition: Reuse applies a suitable existing contract in another context, composition connects compatible contracts into larger behavior, and orchestration coordinates their order, branching, and failure flow.
purpose: Build larger workflows without duplicating rules or creating false generic abstractions.
history: Reuse has often been overemphasized as a goal; contemporary design treats clear responsibility and change evidence as prerequisites for extraction.
mental_model: Small transformations become a pipeline when outputs match later inputs; an orchestrator directs the route without performing every stage's internal work.
analogy: A conductor coordinates specialists but does not play every instrument; software orchestration also manages data and failure contracts absent from the analogy.
industry_notes: Prefer a little duplication over the wrong shared abstraction when responsibilities are still changing independently.
ai_notes: AI-proposed reuse must identify shared invariant, callers, variation points, and contract tests.
interview_notes: Ask when duplication should remain and when composition improves design.
